'''Frederick J. Beutler''' is a [[mathematician]], [[engineer]], and academic. He is a professor emeritus at the [[University of Michigan]].

Beutler's research interests have included [[information theory]], [[electrical engineering]], and [[applied mathematics]], with a focus on [[stochastic process]]es, [[signal processing]], optimization of complex systems, and [[queueing theory]]. He is a life fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE).

== Early life and education==
Beutler was born on October 3, 1926, in Berlin. He was the first child of physicians Alfred David Beutler and Käthe (Italiener) Beutler. His family emigrated to the United States in 1936. He completed his [[Bachelor of Science|S.B.]] and [[Master of Science|S.M.]] degrees from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1949 and 1951, respectively. Later in 1957, he earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name=CV>{{Cite web|url=https://umich.academia.edu/FrederickBeutler/CurriculumVitae|title=Frederick Beutler – Curriculum Vitae|website=Academia.edu|access-date=December 8, 2025}}</ref><ref name=STP/> His doctoral dissertation, ''A generalization of Weiner optimum filtering and prediction'', was supervised by Charles Raymond De Prima.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|233403}}</ref>

==Career==
From 1951 to 1954, Beutler was a research engineer at the Autonetics Division of [[North American Aviation]] (NAA). Subsequently, he worked as a consultant for Ramo-Wooldridge Corp and Lockheed Aircraft until 1957.<ref name=CV/>

At the University of Michigan, Beutler was an assistant professor of Aeronautical Engineering from 1957 to 1959, associate professor of [[Instrumentation]] from 1959 to 1963, professor of Instrumentation from 1963 to 1967, and professor of Information and Control Engineering between 1967 and 1990. Later, he chaired the Computer Information and Control Engineering Program for two distinct periods, from 1970 to 1971 and again from 1977 to 1990. In 1984, he was appointed as a professor of [[Electronic engineering|Electronics Engineering]] and Computer Science, and from the following year, he chaired the Electrical Engineering Systems Graduate Program, positions he held until 1990. Since then, he has been a professor emeritus of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, as well as of Information and Control Engineering. He was the managing editor for the [[SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics|SIAM ''Journal on Applied Mathematics'']] from 1968 to 1973.<ref name=CV/><ref name=STP/>

==Research==
By employing Hilbert space approaches, Beutler showed that perfect reconstruction is attainable for sampling systems with a variation from equal sample intervals of less than 22%<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kuhn |first1=J. R. |title=Recovering spectral information from unevenly sampled data - Two machine-efficient solutions |journal=The Astronomical Journal |date=1982 |volume=87 |pages=196–202 |doi=10.1086/113096 |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1982AJ.....87..196K/abstract }}</ref> and also determined generalizations for other sampling patterns.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Oberti |first1=Sylvain |last2=Correia |first2=Carlos |last3=Fusco |first3=Thierry |last4=Neichel |first4=Benoit |last5=Guiraud |first5=Pierre |title=Super-resolution wavefront reconstruction |journal=Astronomy & Astrophysics |date=2022 |volume=667 |pages=A48 |doi=10.1051/0004-6361/202243954 |url=https://www.aanda.org/articles/aa/full_html/2022/11/aa43954-22/aa43954-22.html}}</ref> He has established a rigorous basis for stationary point processes, elucidated their properties, and studied their applications to communication and control.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Srivastava |first1=Radhendushka |last2=Sengupta |first2=Debasis |title=Effect of Inter-Sample Spacing Constraint on Spectrum Estimation with Irregular Sampling |journal=IEEE Transactions on Information Theory |date=July 2011 |volume=57 |issue=7 |pages=4709–4719 |doi=10.1109/TIT.2011.2146510|arxiv=1004.4686 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Masry |first1=Elias |title=Random sampling and reconstruction of spectra |journal=Information and Control |date=November 1971 |volume=19 |issue=4 |pages=275–288 |doi=10.1016/S0019-9958(71)90146-X}}</ref> Another body of his work has addressed pseudoinverses, extending them to bounded linear [[Banach spaces|Banach space]] with closed ranges.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Djbkovic |first1=I. |last2=Vaidyanathan |first2=P.P. |title=Generalized sampling theorems in multiresolution subspaces |journal=IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing |date=1997 |volume=45 |issue=3 |pages=583–599 |doi=10.1109/78.558473 |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/558473|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Beutler's research on queuing networks led to new results related to optimization of control and service systems.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tidball |first1=Mabel M. |last2=Lombardi |first2=Ariel |last3=Pourtallier |first3=Odile |last4=Altman |first4=Eitan |title=Continuity of Optimal Values and Solutions for Control of Markov Chains with Constraints |journal=SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization |date=January 2000 |volume=38 |issue=4 |pages=1204–1222 |doi=10.1137/S0363012997280294}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stidham |first1=Shaler |last2=Weber |first2=Richard |title=A survey of Markov decision models for control of networks of queues |journal=Queueing Systems |date=March 1993 |volume=13 |issue=1-3 |pages=291–314 |doi=10.1007/BF01158935}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Beutler married Abigail Elaine Caplan in 1951, and they had three children: Arthur David, Kathryn Ruth, and Michael Ernest Beutler. After divorcing Abigail, he married Suzanne Armstrong Ireland in 1969.<ref name=STP>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stolpersteine-berlin.de/en/theodor-heuss-platz/2/friedrich-joseph-beutler|title=Prof. Dr. Friedrich Joseph Beutler|website=Stolpersteine Berlin|access-date=September 24, 2025}}</ref> Later in his career, he worked as a photographer and exhibited his work at exhibitions, including the [[Ann Arbor District Library|Ann Arbor district library]].<ref>{{cite news |title=A cheerful snapshot of an artist's work|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-ann-arbor-news/181986267/ |newspaper=[[The Ann Arbor News]] |date=November 7, 2010 |page=C5 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=September 29, 2025}}</ref>
